name: Albania
summary: Albania taxes residents on worldwide income. Capital gains on shares and real estate are taxed at a flat 15% and dividends at a flat 8%. There is no net wealth tax. Inheritances and gifts between first- and second-order legal heirs (which covers parents to children) are exempt from the 15% inheritance and gift tax. No special tax regime for wealthy arrivals was found. Confidence is medium: this rests mainly on PwC (reviewed July 2026), and the new Income Tax Law No. 29/2023 (in force 1 January 2024) was not read in the original.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Ordinary residence. Residents are taxed on worldwide income under Law No. 29/2023 'On Income Tax' (in force 1 January 2024).
regimes.eligibility: Tax resident with a permanent home in Albania or presence of more than 183 days in the calendar year. Non-citizens need a residence permit.

capital_gains.summary: Capital gains on shares are taxed at 15% (sale price minus purchase price or nominal value). Gains on the sale of land or buildings are also taxed at 15%. Residents are taxed on worldwide income, so gains on foreign securities are in scope.

sources.title: Albania – Individual – Taxes on personal income

open_questions: Whether gains on foreign listed securities are taxed at 15% as 'investment income' or under another category of Law 29/2023 was not confirmed from the statute.
Whether any holding-period or main-residence exemption exists under Law 29/2023 was not verified.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Law No. 29/2023 'On Income Tax' replaced Law 8438/1998 from 1 January 2024; PwC lists no 2025 changes to capital gains.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Flat 15% on the gain for shares and real estate per PwC (reviewed 22 Jul 2026). PwC does not distinguish listed/foreign shares; worldwide taxation is assumed to apply the same rate to foreign gains and foreign real estate.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Residents are taxed on all sources of income in and outside Albania; relief for foreign tax under treaties (42 in force).
capital_gains.professional_trader: Regular trading could be treated as business income (15% up to ALL 14 million, 23% above, 0% for small businesses with turnover up to ALL 14 million until 2029). No specific guidance found.

dividends.summary: Dividends received by individuals are taxed at a flat 8%. Residents are taxed on worldwide income, so foreign dividends are in scope.

sources.title: Albania – Individual – Taxes on personal income

open_questions: Whether foreign dividends are taxed at 8% or as 'other investment income' at 15% was not confirmed from Law 29/2023.
dividends.rate_basis: Flat 8% dividend rate per PwC Taxes on personal income (reviewed 22 Jul 2026), applied to foreign dividends on the assumption that the same rate applies under worldwide taxation.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 8% domestic WHT on dividends to non-residents, reduced by treaty to 5% in many cases.
dividends.treaty_network: 46 treaties signed, 42 in force (PwC), mainly European states plus China, India, Turkey, UAE, Qatar, Singapore, UK. No treaty with the United States.

wealth_tax.summary: Albania has no net wealth tax. Buildings are subject to an annual property tax (residential 0.05% of value per PwC).
wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Annual building tax: residential 0.05% of property value, commercial 0.2% (PwC).

inheritance.summary: Inheritances and gifts are taxed at 15% without deduction of costs, but transfers to and between legal heirs of the first and second order (which includes children) and between siblings are exempt. Children therefore inherit and receive gifts tax-free.
open_questions: The exact statutory article and whether the exemption depends on the heir's residence or registration were not verified.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: Exempt: transfers from or between first- and second-order legal heirs and siblings; otherwise up to ALL 5 million of immovable and ALL 1 million of movable assets exempt.
inheritance.gift_tax: Gifts follow the same rules: 15% in general, exempt between first- and second-order legal heirs.

residency.tax_residency_test: Resident if the individual has a permanent home in Albania or stays more than 183 days in a calendar year (consecutively or not). Treaty rules prevail.

routes.name: Residence permit
routes.requirements: Albania is not in the EU. Foreigners need a residence permit; US citizens historically could stay one year visa-free (not re-verified). Permit grounds were not researched in this pass.

corporate.summary: Standard CIT 15%. Reduced 5% for certain software producers (to end-2025) and agricultural co-operatives/agro-tourism (to end-2029). 8% WHT on outbound dividends.

sources.title: Albania – Corporate – Taxes on corporate income

us_citizen_notes: No US–Albania income tax treaty was found in the PwC treaty list, so US citizens rely on the US foreign tax credit for Albanian tax.
open_questions: Law No. 29/2023 was not read in the original; rates rely on PwC (reviewed July 2026).

prime_rent_monthly.description: Median asking rent (EUR 2,500/month) of the 25 villas for rent in Tirana whose agency reference codes indicate a 2025–26 listing date (range EUR 1,000–10,000), out of 176 villa rentals listed in Real Estate Albania's 'Villa for rent in Tirana' section (12 pages) on 2026-10-15; the median of all 176, including older listings, is EUR 2,000. Bedroom counts are not consistently given, so the sample is villas generally (typically 200–500 m² built, often in Lundër/Long Hill, TEG, Sauk, Farka); some are offered for office use. Agency asking prices, not achieved rents. The reading of reference codes as month-year is our inference. Checked 2026-10-15 against the upper-middle-class standard.

intl_school_annual_fee.description: World Academy of Tirana (IB, Orbital Education), 2026–27: DP1 (age 16) tuition EUR 13,950 plus a EUR 1,000 yearly guarantee fee = EUR 14,950 (DP2 EUR 14,370 + 1,000; MYP EUR 11,350–11,500 + 1,000). One-off EUR 550 registration fee. Meals not included for DP.

cost_of_living.notes: Rent from Real Estate Albania's villa-rental listings (agency site); Century 21 Albania, Merrjep.al and Indomio could not be read. Tirana International School (QSI) does not publish fees.
